clinician.final_diagnosis: Central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) accompanied by ciliary retinal artery (CLRA) occlusion secondary to OCPs
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 28-year-old female presented with sudden painless loss of vision in the left eye. Ophthalmic exam showed left eye counting fingers vision and RAPD with normal anterior segment and intraocular pressure. Fundus exam revealed classic CRVO signs (optic disc edema, preretinal hemorrhages, venous tortuosity, cotton wool spots) plus a white ischemic area suggestive of ciliary retinal artery occlusion. Laboratory evaluation for thrombophilia (PT, aPTT, INR, antiphospholipid antibodies, factor V Leiden mutation) was normal. There were no reports of other hypercoagulability tests or clinical course documentation. The diagnosis was made clinically and supported by fundus findings, with secondary etiology attributed to oral contraceptive pill use.
